Definition: adverb from the same as G170; inopportunely:--out of season.
BiblicalUsage: Once, in Paul's last charge to Timothy: Preach the word; be instant in season, out of season. The word is unseasonable — the wrong time, the inconvenient moment.
TheologicalSignificance: One word for out of season carries little weight on its own; its weight is Paul's charge to Timothy, preach when the room is warm and when it is cold.
